title: What If You Never Showered Again? A Doctor Tried It for 5 Years

scenes.text: What if you stopped showering, forever? A doctor tried it for five years. The smell surprised him.
Your skin carries a living layer of bacteria and fungi that feed on your oils and dead skin. Soap strips it off every morning.
Sweat itself has no smell. The odor comes when bacteria in your armpits feed on it. So at first, yes, you stink.
Dr James Hamblin quit soap, shampoo and deodorant for five years, washing only his hands. A strong oniony smell at first. Then it faded.
His skin got less oily and his eczema flared less. His partner's verdict: he smelled like a person.
Harvard doctors say daily showers don't improve your health and can crack your skin. But one man isn't a study. Nobody is telling you to stop.

description:
What if you never showered again? Your skin carries a microbiome of bacteria, fungi and viruses that live on your oils and shed cells; UCLA Health notes that over-washing with soap and abrasives can strip these colonies away. Sweat itself is odourless; body odour comes from skin bacteria meeting the sweat of the apocrine glands in the armpits and groin.
Physician and author James Hamblin gave up soap, shampoo and deodorant for about five years, still washing his hands, and reported that an initial strong odour faded, his skin became less oily and his eczema improved. Harvard Health says daily showering does not improve health and can leave skin dry and cracked, but a single person's experience is not evidence for everyone. Not medical advice.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: About two thirds of Americans shower every day; in China about half of people say they bathe twice a week. What habit should we switch off next? Drop your own what-if below.
